newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Upbeat South African bonds ended stronger on Thursday after good demand across-the-board fuelled by better U.S. Treasuries and an improved local money market.
At 1608 GMT government's R150 stock was at 15.045 percent from 15.14 percent late on Wednesday an intraday best level of 15.03 percent.
"It's been a good week so far with offshore and local guys keen to buy. Last week there was absolutely no direction in the market," said a senior trader.
Demand was attributed to stronger U.S. bonds which were boosted by initial U.S. claims data. The 30-year U.S. T-bond was last at 7.07 percent from 7.10 percent in late New York trade on Wednesday.
Another positive was a drop in both short-end money market rates and the daily money market shortage which moved to its lowest level in over two months.

Roelf du Plooy, assistant general manager in the Reserve Bank's money and capital market division, said the decline in the shortage had come about as a result of a slight mismatch in government flows.
Bond traders said there was technical resistance at the 15 percent figure level but a test was likely on Friday.
"We got a bit stuck on the way down today but there's a good chance that we will break the figure tomorrow," a second bond trader said.
Option book trading ahead of the May 2 close-out had played a role in 15 percent holding on the downside, he added.

After the dearth of fresh economic news at home which diverted the focus to the U.S. market this week, players were keenly awaiting inflation, money supply and trade numbers -- all due out next week, the dealer said.
Foreigners were net buyers of 155.42 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 494.27 million on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 5.31 billion rand on Wednesday from 4.54 billion rand on Tuesday.
In late trade, the R150 broke below the key 15.00 percent level to trade at 14.97 percent -- its lowest in a month -- as the U.S. Treasury bond's continued strength triggered fresh offshore buying.
On the foreign exchange market, the rand ended little changed from its previous closing levels after good two-way business.
Importer dollar demand initially outweighed exporter supply but in the afternoon the unit retraced some losses.
At 1630 GMT the currency was trading at 4.4580/4610 on a struggling U.S. dollar from 4.4575/4605 overnight.
"There were quite a few importers in the market today but the rand moved in a narrow range and I don't expect any big moves tomorrow," a forex dealer said.
He said there had been a lot of stability in the market during the week despite a strong U.S. dollar. Friday's direction would most likely be dictated by local bonds which were looking healthy.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 28.2152/2410 yen from 28.1883/2253 yen, 0.3868/3873 marks from 0.3874/3879 marks and 7.2593/2686 rand against sterling from 7.2293/2386 rand.

On the money market, leading banks all quoted their three-month NCDs rates lower at 16.55 percent offered from between 16.60 to 16.65 percent previously after the Reserve Bank reported the shortage fell to 7.853 billion rand on Wednesday from 8.411 billion rand.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
